thread.title: Coherent Tumbles As Laser Maker Points To Disappointing Outlook

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Coherent Tumbles As Laser Maker Points To Disappointing Outlook
text:
Laser systems maker Coherent ( COHR ) fell hard on Thursday after it posted slightly better-than-expected December-quarter results, but disappointed with its profit outlook.
Coherent shares plunged 17.4% to close at 205.89 on the stock market today . The stock has been on a downward trajectory since hitting an all-time high of 329 on Jan. 19, breaking out of a seven-week consolidation period with a buy point of 320.83.
Since reaching its zenith, Coherent has fallen for 14 of the last 16 trading sessions. It slashed through its 50-day moving average line, a bearish technical sign, in heavy trading on Jan. 23. Things worsened on Feb. 1, when it undercut its 200-day moving average.
Santa Clara, Calif.-based Coherent late Wednesday reported adjusted earnings per share of $3.54, up 38% year over year, on sales of $478 million, also up 38%, in its fiscal first quarter ended Dec. 30. Analysts expected earnings of $3.52 a share on sales of $474 million.
"The sharp correction in Coherent shares is likely to continue today after the company posted slightly better fiscal Q1 results, but provided a lower-than-expected guide for fiscal Q2 margins, due to the negative impact from the stronger euro," Needham analyst James Ricchiuti said in a note to clients Thursday.
Ricchiuti reiterated his buy rating on Coherent, but slashed his price target on the stock to 295 from 330.

Coherent's laser systems are used in a broad range of scientific, commercial and industrial applications. One of the company's big growth drivers recently has been lasers used in the manufacture of OLED displays.
On a conference call with analysts, Coherent management expressed confidence in the underlying strength of the display business, Ricchiuti said.
"Management addressed concerns about the OLED capacity buildout and overall utilization of its equipment in the field in the wake of disappointing ( Apple ( AAPL )) iPhone X demand," Ricchiuti said. "Coherent said that there has been no change in the timing of shipment deliveries by customers, nor has there been hesitancy among the newer players in China to go through the qualifications and early scale-up of OLED fabs that are in the startup mode."
Coherent stock also received price-target cuts from Stifel and Susquehanna Financial Group, both of which maintained buy ratings.
Ichor Falls On December-Quarter Report Elsewhere in the display and semiconductor capital equipment market, Ichor Holdings ( ICHR ) stock plunged 16.5% to close at 22.01, after the company posted fourth-quarter results late Wednesday.
Ichor topped estimates for fourth-quarter earnings per share by a penny, but missed views by a penny with its outlook for the current quarter.
Ichor reported adjusted earnings per share of 70 cents, up 43% year over year, on sales of $183 million, up 39%, in the December quarter. Analysts expected 69 cents and $183 million, according to Zacks Investment Research.
For the current quarter, Ichor expects to earn an adjusted 94 cents a share, up 65% year over year, on sales of $245 million, up 64%, based on the midpoint of its guidance. Wall Street was modeling 95 cents and $245 million.
Fremont, Calif.-based Ichor designs and manufactures fluid delivery subsystems for semiconductor capital equipment.
"We believe Ichor can sustain double-digit sales growth reflecting a confluence of better demand trends within memory (especially deposition and etch) and ability to sustain share gains across both gas and chemical delivery," RBC Capital Markets analyst Amit Daryanani said in a report Thursday.
Ichor has about 26% share in gas delivery systems and 9% share in chemical delivery systems, he said.
The market remains fragmented and Ichor has opportunities to consolidate it through mergers and acquisitions, Daryanani said.
